f: National Financial Partners was an independent broker where Jonathan McQuade began his career in practice management consulting after college, starting in 2007. At NFP, he worked on the practice management team, providing support services to independent wealth management owners throughout the NFP network. His role involved guiding these firm owners on how to operate more efficiently across all areas of practice management, including hiring and human capital management, balance sheet and P&L management, and strategic vision for building larger and better firms. This position gave McQuade valuable exposure to the wealth management industry by allowing him to visit firm owners across the country and observe the many different ways businesses could be operated in the field.

McQuade's time at NFP was disrupted when the financial crisis hit in 2008-2009 and the company's stock dropped below a dollar, resulting in his entire team being eliminated and leaving him without work. However, this initial experience proved instrumental in shaping his career trajectory, as it exposed him to industry operations from a consulting perspective before he eventually transitioned into advisory roles. After a brief stint at Charles Schwab's Retirement Plan Department, he returned to practice management work with Fusion Advisor Network and later the Ensemble Practice, gaining additional experience before ultimately deciding to pursue a career as a wealth advisor rather than a consultant.
